source.title: Local proxies for memory-efficient training
source.authors: Wu-Zi S. Han; Brian A. Yuan; G. Bellec

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including main text and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains vision transformers on CIFAR-100 and fine-tunes language models with local proxy propagation, reporting accuracy and resource comparisons. Those results extend the setting to local gradient methods but do not measure whether gradient training from random initialization reaches near-zero training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training and evaluation outcomes for ProxyProp, backpropagation, and other local methods. Its accuracy results are test or task performance, not training classification error; no result tests V1–V6. No rows meet the claim-version measurement rules.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual architecture and zeroed residual initialization to construct accurate local gradient estimates, then evaluates ProxyProp's gradient alignment, task performance, memory and compute. These results do not measure any V1–V6 outcome. In particular, gradient alignment at initialization is not training speed or trainable depth, and CIFAR-100 test accuracy is not training classification error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that ProxyProp provides memory-efficient local gradient estimates with conditional theoretical guarantees and achieves near-backpropagation task performance in ViT training and LLM fine-tuning. Exactness in linear networks requires the stated assumptions and an optimal proxy; the nonlinear residual error bound requires skip-dominated networks. ProxyProp is approximately 1.5 times slower per step than backpropagation in the reported LLM comparison, while outperforming the cited MeZO results with less compute.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates local proxy-gradient propagation for memory-efficient training and fine-tuning, rather than the original claim's end-to-end gradient-training error outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported accuracy varies with the number of network blocks, proxy form, task and model; these are not measurements of the claim versions' named behaviors.

fits_no_version.finding: Remark 3.3 and Figure 2 show exact initial ProxyProp gradients when both the residual network and proxy are initialized to identity; Figures 2–3 measure improvements in gradient alignment from proxy fitting and residual parameterization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual proxy parameterization and distillation can improve local estimates of backpropagation gradients.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports CIFAR-100 test accuracy of 64.90±0.44% for ProxyProp with three blocks versus 66.13% for backpropagation, with peak memory of 4.64 versus 12.30 GB. These are method-performance comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local proxy propagation can approach backpropagation's test accuracy while reducing activation memory.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 and Table A3 report language-model fine-tuning task performance and resource costs; Table A3 gives SQuAD performance of 84.75±0.91 for ProxyProp versus 88.30±0.82 for backpropagation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ProxyProp offers a task-performance and memory trade-off for language-model fine-tuning.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says implementation will be published on GitHub upon acceptance.
record.problems: Results relevant to the catalog claim are not reported: the paper gives last-epoch or test-task accuracy rather than training classification error, and does not test the specified mechanisms or training conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The reported outcomes concern accuracy, memory and compute, and do not measure a claim-version behavior under the row rules.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including random or corrupted labels and comparisons with smaller or regularized models.
Spurious local minima frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with increasing plain-network depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified deep plain or normalization-free residual training results.
Effects of activation-matched initialization and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights on learning speed or trainable depth.
Loss recovery, curvature changes, divergence and edge-of-stability dynamics relative to a learning-rate stability threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable normalization-free training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification conflicts with its own gate note and should be corrected to uses_without_test/T4. Keeping the row set empty is appropriate. Residual-versus-non-residual proxy ablations do not test depth degradation in plain versus residual backbone networks.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error, zero or corrupted labels, or the specified CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training-error comparisons.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem, spurious-minima frequency, or teacher/student width sweep.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison measuring training error, and no test of very deep plain networks or normalization-free residual training.
No comparison of initialization schemes for training speed or trainable depth.
No learning-rate stability threshold, loss-rise/recovery, sharpness, or divergence measurement.
No batch-normalization versus no-normalization comparison measuring training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
